claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a homogeneous single-phase BCC structure.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
Approximately half of the Hf should be replaced by Nb to form Hf0.5Nb0.5MoTaTiZr.
Casting under inert atmosphere followed by homogenization will produce a uniform single-phase BCC alloy.
The Nb-modified alloy will maintain a single-phase BCC solid solution.
Maintaining the BCC solid solution will preserve the existing solid-solution-strengthening mechanisms.
Hf has an atomic weight of approximately 178, whereas Nb has an atomic weight of approximately 93.
Replacing Hf with lighter Nb will reduce the alloy's mass per unit volume.
Nb has refractory properties and strengthening effects comparable to those of the Hf it replaces.
Nb's refractory properties and comparable strengthening effects will preserve the alloy's mechanical performance.
A uniform BCC structure will provide effective load transfer across the stated temperature range.
A uniform BCC structure will hinder dislocation motion across the stated temperature range.
The modified alloy's density could approach approximately 9 g/cm³.
The modified alloy will retain high room-temperature yield strength.
The modified alloy will retain room-temperature ductility.
The modified alloy will retain mechanical performance under quasi-static loading up to approximately 1000 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has proven high strength and ductility at room and elevated temperatures.
The expected performance range is from room temperature to approximately 1000 °C under conventional loading conditions.
Retention of performance during prolonged high-temperature exposure depends on the alloy remaining homogeneous and phase-stable.

contradictions.description: The modified material is described as as-cast, but the prescribed state includes a subsequent homogenization heat treatment; an alloy after homogenization is not strictly in the as-cast condition.
